transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… thanks for seeing me. I guess what finally made me ask for help is that I’ve been forgetting small things I usually manage okay—like returning calls, turning in a registration form, or remembering to stop for an errand on the way home. It’s not, you know, anything huge, but it’s been happening enough that I thought I should probably talk to someone.
Did you have trouble paying attention as a child?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I wasn’t a bad student or anything, I don’t think, but even in elementary school I was kind of the kid who’d forget permission slips or lose my homework somewhere in my backpack. Projects were hard for me to finish unless my mom or the teacher sort of walked me through it step by step and reminded me what to do next. Does that count as trouble paying attention?
Do these kinds of attention or organization problems cause trouble for you at work?

A little, yeah. I mean, I’m still getting by at work—I don’t think anyone would say I’m failing or anything—but I have missed small follow-ups, like forgetting to call someone back or not circling back on something until later than I should.

And I’ve had some school-related deadlines too that I didn’t handle as well as I wanted. It makes me nervous, honestly, because I’d like to be seen as reliable and maybe move into an Office Manager role eventually. I worry if these little things keep happening, it could hurt how people see me. Does that make sense?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different things?

I don’t think so… not a lot, anyway. I mean, I worry about normal things, like work stuff or if I’ve forgotten something, but I wouldn’t say it’s about many different things all the time. Unless I’m not understanding exactly what you mean?
Do these kinds of forgetting or organization problems also happen at home?

Yeah… it does, though I try to keep on top of things. It’s usually little stuff, not anything huge, but like I’ll mean to return a call and then it just slips, or I’ll forget to turn in a registration form, or I’ll be driving home and completely forget I was supposed to stop for an errand.

Honestly, that’s kind of what finally made me think maybe I should ask for help. It’s embarrassing because these are normal things I feel like I should be able to handle.
Have these forgetting and organization problems been present pretty consistently since childhood?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, because I did okay overall, but even in elementary school I was kind of that kid who forgot permission slips or had homework somewhere in my backpack and couldn’t find it.

I remember needing my mom, or sometimes the teacher, to sort of walk me through projects step by step or remind me what came next. I guess I always thought that was just me being scattered, if that makes sense.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Not really, no. I mean, I have days where I feel frustrated with myself, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been depressed lately. I don’t think so, anyway.
Did these problems get noticeably worse after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

Not after something bad, exactly. I mean, nothing dramatic happened. It’s just… since I started this evening certificate program, about 15 months ago, it’s been harder to keep everything managed.

I don’t want to make it sound like I fell apart or anything, but that’s when I noticed the forgetting and staying organized started taking more effort than before. Does that make sense?
When you sit down to focus, do you often find that worry gets in the way?

Um… I don’t think worry is usually the main thing, no. I mean, I might get a little stressed if I know I’m behind, but when I sit down it’s more like my mind just doesn’t stay on the thing very well.

I’m not sure if that answers it the right way. It doesn’t feel like I’m sitting there worrying the whole time, if that makes sense.
When you’re trying to do something that needs focus, do you get distracted easily?

Yeah… I do, somewhat. I mean, I try not to, and it’s not like I can’t focus at all, but at work or in class if a phone rings, or people are talking nearby, I can lose my place pretty easily.

Sometimes it’s even just a random thought, like something I need to do at home, and then I realize I’m not really on the task anymore. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often put off tasks that require a lot of sustained mental effort?

Yeah… I do, probably more than I should. I don’t mean to be lazy or anything, but if something means I have to sit down and read a long chapter or write out a whole plan, I tend to push it off.

Then it gets late, and I end up rushing through it after work, which isn’t ideal. I usually get it done, but not in the calm, organized way I wish I did. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Do you often feel restless, like it’s hard to sit still?

A little, yeah. I wouldn’t say I’m up and pacing around or anything, but during longer classes I’ll notice I’m clicking my pen or bouncing my foot, or kind of shifting around in the chair even when I’m trying to sit still and pay attention.

It’s not extreme, I don’t think… but it does happen. Is that what you mean by restless?
When someone is speaking to you directly, do you often realize afterward that you missed part of what they said?

Um… I don’t know if I’d say often. Maybe once in a while I’ll realize I didn’t catch everything, especially if I’m tired or there’s a lot going on, but I try to listen.

Sometimes I’ll kind of nod along and then think, “Wait, what did they just say?” But I don’t know if that’s more than normal. Is that what you mean?
Do you often misplace things you need, like keys, papers, or your phone?

Yeah… I do, unfortunately. I try to keep things in the same place, but I’m always setting down my planner or my flash drive or keys somewhere, and then I’m checking my purse, my car, my office drawers… it can take ten minutes before I can move on.

It’s not like I lose them permanently, usually, but it does slow me down. Does that count as misplacing things?
When you forget things, is it usually because the information never really stuck in your mind in the first place?

Yeah, I think that’s probably true sometimes. Like, I’ll fully intend to do something, but it’s like it never really gets planted firmly in my head.

That’s actually kind of what made me finally ask for help. I kept forgetting small things I normally should be able to handle—returning a phone call, turning in a registration form, stopping for an errand on the way home. Nothing huge, but enough that I started feeling embarrassed and worried I was dropping the ball. Does that make sense?
If someone reminds you of the thing you forgot, does it usually come back to you right away?

Usually, yes. If someone says, “Don’t forget the registration form,” or “Did you return that call?” I’ll be like, oh—right, yes, I meant to do that.

It’s not that I don’t care, it’s more like little things I normally handle just slip out of my head, like returning calls or stopping for an errand on the way home. That’s actually kind of what made me ask about it, because it started happening enough that I felt embarrassed. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Outside of work and school, do you also have these attention and organization problems in other parts of your life?

Yes, I think it shows up outside of work too… not in a dramatic way, but enough that it’s frustrating.

Like, what finally made me ask for help was realizing I kept forgetting little things I normally handle—returning calls, turning in a registration form, or remembering to stop for an errand on the way home. They’re small things, so I feel a little silly bringing them up, but they’ve been happening enough that I noticed.
